topComments.author: drfuchs
topComments.text: For prior related work, check out patent US-6377261-B1 "Compiling glyphs into instructions for imaging for execution on a general purpose computer" filed 1996. The basic idea is each character turns into a sequence of "Load Immediate" / "Shift" / "OR to Memory" instructions; so there's no more fetching from a stored bitmap of the font, as the pixels are implicit in the Immediate data in the generated machine code. Then you can get fancy when one row of pixels is the same as the previous row in the character, so you don't even need to do the Load Immediate. Etc. This scheme was used in FrameMaker for Macintosh back in the day, as implemented by Gus Fernandez (who went hog wild on additional optimizations).

topComments.author: codazoda
topComments.text: I've been building BASIC32, a retro BASIC interpreter for microcontrollers so I can flash it once and easily create lots of new projects. What you give up with the authors approach is "read". The screen becomes write-only. There are only a few functions that require reads: getting a pixels current color and doing operations like flood fills or paints. Because I was going for the retro feel of BASIC, I wanted to support these, so I opted for a frame buffer. It isn't as technically cool. On the RP2350, it does require low resolution and low bit rates because they often have RAM limited to KB. If you step-up to the ESP32-S3 variants with 4MB or 8MB of RAM the frame buffer gets much easier.

However, I get time limit exceeded in 2 tests, so it needs more optimization, I would say but cannot figure out how now. Could you help me where and how to optimize? P.S.: We are only allowed to use SSE2 for some paralelism. Assignment: Inverted File An inverted file (IVF) splits the points into clusters, keeps one list of points per cluster, and searches only the clusters that can contain the answer. Building: Choose k cluster centres with k-means: start with k random points as the centres, then a few times assign every point to its nearest centre and move every centre to the mean of its points. k around √n is a good start. The k-means clustering might be too expensive, but you can run it on a sample of points. Assign every point to its nearest centre, and store the points of each cluster next to each other. For each cluster, remember its radius R: the largest distance from its centre to one of its points. Searching for q: For each cluster with centre c and radius R, compute a lower bound d(q, c) − R. By the triangle inequality, no point of the cluster is nearer to q than that. Go through the clusters in order of their bound, and compare q with every point of each one. Stop as soon as the bound of the next cluster is larger than the distance to the nearest point found so far: no point in that cluster or any later one can be nearer. IVF is also used for approximate nearest neighbour search, which looks only at a few of the nearest clusters. That is faster but sometimes wrong; here the answers must be exact, so step 3 stops only when none of the remaining clusters can contain a nearer point. stackOverflowQuestions.title: Remove all characters between brackets and the brackets as well from file names
stackOverflowQuestions.bodyExcerpt: I have a lot of file(s) that have random text between square brackets eg: [a9b7a=9sd09] and would like a quick way to remove the text and the brackets from all files within a certain directory. The text between brackets is always random and I've looked at sed substitution, rename (Python script), krename and other ideas but I haven't had any luck yet. Most one liners get complaints from fish shell and therefore most scripts I try fail. I've come from How do I Remove Specific Characters From File Names Using BASH and Removing special characters from file names bash script and other posts like this which are roughly the same in concept but fish won't accept them, so I'm stuck. I know I could drop back to bash shell but there are a lot of files and I'm always adding to my collection and would love a fast way to do this. So the basic idea is to identify the characters for removal i.e.: '[' and ']' and any wild cards in between with possible leading '/' trailing white spaces. Being able to specify the type of brackets or characters for that matter would be a bonus.

stackOverflowQuestions.title: t-string HTML renderer ignores `:.2f` and escapes nested templates as raw text
stackOverflowQuestions.bodyExcerpt: I’m switching my HTML helpers from f-strings to t-strings so user input gets escaped automatically. Escaping works, but number formatting is gone. When I put one template inside another, the inner template comes out as an escaped object dump instead of HTML. from string.templatelib import Template, Interpolation import html def render(template: Template) -> str: parts = [] for item in template: if isinstance(item, Interpolation): parts.append(html.escape(str(item.value))) else: parts.append(item) return "".join(parts) name = "Rahum" price = 19.999 row = t"{name}${price:.2f}" page = t"{row}" print(render(row)) print(render(page)) What I expected: <b>Rahum</b>$20.00 <b>Rahum</b>$20.00 What happened instead (Python 3.14.6): <b>Rahum</b>$19.999 Template(strings=('<td>', '</td><td>$', '</td>'), interpolations=(Interpolation('<b>Rahum</b>', 'name', None, ''), Interpolation(19.999, 'price', None, '.2f'))) Questions: Why is :.2f ignored? With an f-string, the same code prints $20.00 . Why does the nested row template turn into a Template(...) repr instead of rendering? How should render handle format specs, !r / !s conversions, and nested templates without double-escaping the inner HTML? Related question: This answer about t-string logging shows how to apply conversions and format specifications, but does not address nested HTML templates or double escaping.

infoqArticles.title: Entire's Git Forge Rethinks Git Collaboration for Coding Agents
infoqArticles.description: Entire is a Git forge designed specifically for collaboration between human developers and AI coding agents. Its premise is that traditional software development infrastructure, particularly the pull request (PR) model, is not well suited to an environment where AI agents generate, review, and iterate on code at high speed. By Sergio De Simone
infoqArticles.author: Sergio De Simone

infoqArticles.title: Google Cloud Adds Self-Managed VMware Cloud Foundation on Bare Metal
infoqArticles.description: Google Cloud has made a self-managed VMware solution generally available, running VMware Cloud Foundation 9.x on dedicated Z3 bare metal with root access across ESXi, vCenter and NSX in 22 regions. It sits beside the Google-managed VMware Engine and matches customer-operated offerings from AWS and Oracle, shifting lifecycle, patching and Broadcom licensing back to the customer. By Steef-Jan Wigger
infoqArticles.author: Steef-Jan Wiggers

infoqArticles.title: Cloudflare Scales D1 Control Plane to Millions of Databases
infoqArticles.description: In a recent article, Cloudflare shared the redesign of the control plane of its D1 serverless SQL database to support millions of databases, avoiding centralized bottlenecks, implementing retries and idempotency, and using eventual consistency. By Renato Losio
infoqArticles.author: Renato Losio

infoqArticles.title: How Grab Improved Mobile App Stability by Safely Handling Surge in AI-Generated Code Changes
infoqArticles.description: The growing adoption of AI coding assistants has accelerated development and increased the volume of code changes per release, bringing more opportunities for defects and crashes, says Grab. To address these challenges, they implemented a layered defense strategy to prevent, detect, and contain crashes throughout the development and release lifecycle. By Sergio De Simone
infoqArticles.author: Sergio De Simone

infoqArticles.title: Open Source pg_vectorsearch Brings More Scalable Vector Search to PostgreSQL
infoqArticles.description: Tiger Data has released pg_vectorsearch, an open source PostgreSQL extension for vector similarity search, currently in alpha. Its PRISM index uses data partitioning and compression instead of the graph-based approach used by pgvector’s HNSW index, reducing memory requirements and index build times. By Renato Losio
infoqArticles.author: Renato Losio

infoqArticles.title: Varlock Releases Bumpy: A File-Based Versioning Alternative to Changesets
infoqArticles.description: Bumpy is an MIT-licensed, TypeScript tool for version management and changelogs in monorepos. It follows the changesets workflow, using markdown bump files, and adds support for workspace and catalog protocols, custom publish commands, and branch-based prereleases. Changesets v3, released in August 2026, closed many earlier gaps, though differences remain. By Daniel Curtis
infoqArticles.author: Daniel Curtis

infoqArticles.title: Yelp Combines Native and Server-Driven UI for Its AI Assistant
infoqArticles.description: Yelp combines native mobile controls with server-driven conversation rendering in its AI Assistant using the CHAOS framework. The architecture separates view configuration from conversation data, supports backend-driven chat interactions, and enables faster UI updates without new app releases. Yelp also discusses cross-platform challenges and reuse for its Biz Ask Anything pilot. By Leela Kumili
infoqArticles.author: Leela Kumili

infoqArticles.title: GitLab 19.5 Makes Agentic Development a Governed Part of the DevOps Platform
infoqArticles.description: GitLab 19.5, released on October 15, puts agentic software development and governance at the centre of the platform, making its GitLab MCP server generally available while expanding how external AI agents can interact with GitLab. By Craig Risi
infoqArticles.author: Craig Risi

infoqArticles.title: TypeScript 7.1 Beta: Restores the Compiler API and Makes Vue and Svelte First-Class
infoqArticles.description: TypeScript 7.1 Beta, announced October 20, 2026, restores the compiler API removed in 7.0, now split into separate entry points. It adds content mappers, letting tools like Vue check non-standard files. One Vue project's type checks fell from 14.19 to 3.10 seconds. An editor issue remains open, and teams may need TypeScript 6 alongside 7. By Daniel Curtis
infoqArticles.author: Daniel Curtis

infoqArticles.title: Presentation: The Socio-Technical Staff+ Engineer: Architecture, Culture and Organisational Change
infoqArticles.description: Vanessa Formicola shares how technical leaders can move beyond "wishful architecture" by practicing holistic socio-technical engineering. She discusses why engineering leaders must account for organizational maturity, reward structures, geopolitical climate, and team dynamics, framing the staff-plus role as designing the conditions for technology to thrive rather than just picking tools. By Vaness
infoqArticles.author: Vanessa Formicola

infoqArticles.title: AWS Ships Continuum for Code Vulnerabilities
infoqArticles.description: AWS has made Continuum for code vulnerabilities generally available in two regions. The service proves exploitability by running real exploits in a sandbox, then opens fixes as pull requests. Published pricing charges per finding processed as well as per line of code, and practitioners are asking what would justify letting it merge fixes on its own. By Steef-Jan Wiggers
infoqArticles.author: Steef-Jan Wiggers

infoqArticles.title: Article: Identity as an Architectural Concern: Enterprise IAM Beyond Authentication
infoqArticles.description: The way you design your identities will drive your data models, your service scope, and your revocation policies; enterprise identity management is thus an architectural problem, not an afterthought. Based on our experience in service account governance, this article touches upon graph vs. RBAC, integrating a vault you don't own, and bounding revocation latency for an event stream. By Vaishnavi Kh
infoqArticles.author: Vaishnavi Khosla

infoqArticles.title: Vault Fork OpenBao Adds External Keys and Quantum-Ready TLS
infoqArticles.description: OpenBao has released version 2.7, adding read scaling for PostgreSQL-backed deployments, support for external hardware security module (HSM) and key management service (KMS) keys, and post-quantum cryptographic algorithms. The release also introduces control groups for human review of sensitive operations and new headers intended to keep requests consistent across load-balanced OpenBao nodes. By M
infoqArticles.author: Matt Saunders

infoqArticles.title: GitHub Actions Lockfiles Reach GA to Secure Workflow Dependencies
infoqArticles.description: GitHub has made workflow dependency lockfiles for GitHub Actions generally available on October 28, 2026, two weeks after the feature entered public preview. Workflows can maintain clear tag and branch references. By Claudio Masolo
infoqArticles.author: Claudio Masolo

infoqArticles.title: Edera's Object Capability Bounded Authority Promises to Isolate Credentials from AI Agent Workloads
infoqArticles.description: Edera announced Object Capability Bounded Authority, a security model that separates an AI agent's or MCP server's required authority from the credentials behind it. Hypervisor-enforced capabilities limit agents to specific actions without storing secrets in the workload. Initial releases cover scoped command execution and workload identity; credential-brokered API access will follow. By Olimpiu P
